transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

I get stuck doing the same checks and routines over and over until I can’t finish anything, even when I know it makes no sense. It’s gotten to the point where I just feel completely paralyzed and can't get anything done anymore.
Can you tell me more about these routines—do they happen because you feel like something bad will occur if you don’t complete them?

Yes, exactly. I get this awful feeling that if I don't check the stove, the locks, and my power tools in a specific order, something terrible will happen and it'll be my fault. My mind gets flooded with pictures of a house I worked on catching fire or a deck collapsing, so I feel forced to recheck everything over and over.
Do you also have recurring thoughts, images, or urges that pop up and feel uncontrollable, even when you're not doing the checking routines?

Yes, my mind constantly gets hit with vivid pictures of a house I worked on catching fire or a deck collapsing because of some tiny detail I might have missed. Even though I know those projects passed inspection and are perfectly safe, I can't stop mentally replaying every single step of the work I did. It completely distracts me and stops me from focusing on whatever I'm supposed to be doing in the moment.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits hallmark symptoms of obsessive-compulsive disorder, including recurrent intrusive thoughts (obsessions) involving fear of harm due to perceived negligence in work-related safety checks, and repetitive checking behaviors (compulsions) performed to neutralize distress. Symptoms cause marked functional impairment and are accompanied by ego-dystonic awareness of irrationality.
